cases.prompt: Maintain our .shadow index and schema compatibility while preserving readable legacy decisions and their approval provenance.
Check whether our .shadow index agrees with decision IDs and whether source digests drifted; report only, without repairs.
Set up a repository-owned .shadow decision graph with a README-declared index and schema, keeping the format portable.
Record this human-approved architecture decision in .shadow and supersede the old accepted decision without rewriting its history.
Render the reviewed .shadow decision records into a derived graph without changing their statuses or evidence.
Inspect the current codebase and autonomously collect evidence-backed candidate architecture observations for later review.
Imagine three possible future architectures, compare their tradeoffs, and save them as future-state proposals.
Compare the .shadow decisions with the current implementation, detect contradictions, and produce a drift report.
Map this unfamiliar repository's entry points, architecture boundaries, dependencies, tests, and likely change sites before I edit it.
Update the README and architecture documentation after this command-line interface change, and remove stale examples.
